[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: in maths a variable like the i in a sum ranges over all its values at once, and 'i from 1 to 10' is a set. A Java loop variable is one storage location holding one value at a time, changed step by step by the update.
[1] misconception (M) -> LoopUpdateChangesDirection: wrong rule: The update of the loop variable can change from pass to pass (e.g. switch direction) although the code is the same. Right rule: The update expression is the same on every pass; the loop variable changes by the rule written in the update.
[2] misconception (M) -> BodyChangeIgnoredByCondition: wrong rule: Changing the loop variable inside the body does not affect the loop condition; the loop still runs its planned number of times. Right rule: The condition is tested with the current value of the variable, including changes made in the body.
[3] misconception (M) -> LoopOutputSameEachPass: wrong rule: A loop prints the same thing on every pass; the changing loop variable does not affect what the body does. Right rule: The body uses the current value of the loop variable, so its output can differ on each pass.
[4] misconception (M) -> LoopVariableLimitsValues: wrong rule: The range of the loop variable limits the values that can be read or printed inside the loop. Right rule: The loop variable only counts passes; other values read or printed in the body are not bounded by it.
[5] inconsistent_trace (T) -> LoopUpdateChangesDirection: Applies the init-test-update rule (LT, loop_control) unevenly to the loop variable: forgets one update, applies a different step on some passes, or re-initializes it mid-loop. (here mixing in: "The update of the loop variable can change from pass to pass (e.g. switch direction) although the code is the same")
[6] misconception (M) -> LoopVariableLifetimeScope: wrong rule: The for variable i is a new variable on every pass rather than one variable changed by the update. Right rule: The for variable i is created once by the init, the update changes that same variable on every pass, and i exists only until the end of the for statement.
[7] misconception (M) -> DoubleLoopIndexCount: wrong rule: for (double x = 0.0; x <= 1.0; x += 0.1) runs exactly 11 times. Right rule: Using a double as a for-loop index is legal but bad practice: the number of iterations depends on an equality test between double values, which may not give the result you expect.
[8] misconception (M) -> ForInitRepeats: wrong rule: The initialization of a for loop runs again after a pass of the body. Right rule: The initialization runs exactly once, before the first condition test.

[0] names_the_element (N): A loop variable (loop-control counter, index) is a variable that is initialized, tested and updated in order to control a loop.
[1] states_the_rule (S): The loop variable is set once by the initialization, tested by the continuation condition before each pass and updated (usually incremented) at the end of each pass; declared in a for header, it is not available after the loop.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Its value is set by the init, read by the test, read by the body, then changed by the update, and the cycle repeats; the body sees the value set by the previous update.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Across passes the loop variable takes a predictable sequence of values, e.g. 4, 5, ..., 10 in TenHellos, and after a while loop it holds the first value that failed the test (11).
[2] one_step_execution (OS): One update changes only the loop variable (i = i + 1 turns 4 into 5); one test reads it and yields true or false; an assignment to it in the body changes what the next test sees.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): The init, condition and update all act on the loop variable: the init sets it, the condition tests it, the update changes it.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): In a while loop the loop variable is declared and initialized before the loop and updated inside the body, so it remains available after the loop.
[2] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Role: stepper - a variable stepping through a systematic, predictable succession of values; it counts passes and often serves as an index.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> LoopUpdateChangesDirection: Shifting the start and the bound by the same amount keeps the number of passes but changes the values the body sees; assigning to the loop variable inside the body changes the pass count.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use a dedicated loop variable (int) when passes are counted or indexed; do not use a double loop variable, and do not reuse it for other roles inside the body.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Update the loop variable only in the update part (or in one place in a while body). Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: An extra i++ in the body (or modifying i elsewhere): passes are skipped or repeated, and the loop may overshoot an != bound and never end.
